source_title: Code Mode — A New Software Architecture for AI Agents
speaker: Sunil Pai (AI Agents team at Cloudflare; creator of PartyKit)
key_insight: Code Mode replaces JSON tool calling with sandboxed code execution against a capability-bounded environment — agents stop dispatching tool calls and start 'inhabiting state machines', with the Cloudflare API reduced from 1.2M tokens (2,600 tools) to 1K tokens (2 tools: search + execute).

PartyKit — Pai's previous open-source project; real-time multiplayer framework on Cloudflare Durable Objects. Establishes the 'one Durable Object per user/room' pattern that informs how Pai thinks about per-user state machines for Code Mode.

discovered_urls.context: V8 isolates documentation — the sandbox runtime Cloudflare uses for Code Mode. Pai cites <5ms startup and 10 years of Chrome security hardening. Worth a dedicated reference doc in infrastructure/.

Kenton Varda — creator of Cloudflare Workers and protagonist of the tic-tac-toe 'inhabiting the state machine' anecdote. He built the wipe coding environment Pai demos. Worth tracking as a practitioner of agent-native tooling.

discovered_urls.context: Deno — alternative capability-based JavaScript/TypeScript runtime with explicit --allow-net, --allow-read, etc. Most actionable Code Mode implementation path for our tmux orchestrator since it runs locally without Cloudflare infrastructure.

cross_references.relation: Direct conceptual complement — Lopopolo argues 'the harness is the product'; Pai provides the runtime architecture. Read as the architectural pair of AIE Europe 2026.
Steinberger warns about unnerfed-Codex sandbox escapes (5 in 30 min); Pai's capability-based sandbox with default-deny network and explicit bindings is the architectural response.
Ubl flags harness/exec co-location as the 1999-era security anti-pattern. Pai's Code Mode sandbox is the fix. Ubl + Pai + Sally Omali (containers) form a coherent 2026 security critique-and-response.

Omali frames containers as the trust boundary for OpenClaw; Pai argues V8 isolates + capability-based security are the finer-grained primitive. Both responses to the same trust-boundary problem at different layers.
Harrison Chase & Sam Partee argue harness + tool runtime = general purpose agent. Pai deepens this: the tool runtime should be a capability-bounded code execution sandbox, not a JSON dispatch layer.

Wattenberger explores canvas-based post-IDE interfaces. Pai's tic-tac-toe anecdote with Kenton's wipe coding environment is an instance of this category (and a TLDraw-style canvas is explicitly mentioned).
Lopopolo's OpenAI harness-engineering manifesto; Pai's Code Mode is compatible architecture for Codex-style agent fleets.

key_concepts.code_mode: Replace JSON tool calling with a single code-string execution against a sandboxed environment. Agent writes JavaScript (or equivalent), harness runs it with only the explicitly granted capabilities.
key_concepts.inhabiting_state_machines: Agent becomes a resident of a state machine rather than a dispatcher of tool calls about the state. Tic-tac-toe demo: no game code, model reads stroke array, recognizes tic-tac-toe, draws circle to play. Ghost-in-the-Shell reference.
key_concepts.two_tool_reduction: For large API surfaces, expose only search(query) + execute(code). Cloudflare API: 2,600 endpoints = 1.2M tokens as MCP tools; reduced to 1,000 tokens (99.9% reduction).
key_concepts.capability_based_security: No ambient authority. Sandbox starts with zero capabilities; only explicitly granted APIs work. From Lisp/E-language tradition. V8 isolates, Wasm, Python, Deno, Lisp all support this model.
key_concepts.sandbox_attributes: Ephemeral, fast-startup (<5ms V8 isolates), default-deny network, full observability/replay, embeddable (run on user device), explicit capability bindings, hostable.
key_concepts.harness_is_the_product: The model is interchangeable; the harness is the moat. Capabilities flow into the sandbox; the sandbox is the actual product surface. Aligns with Lopopolo's harness engineering thesis.
key_concepts.agent_dx: Your next billion users are little robots generating code. They dream in types and syntax errors. Build markdown docs, errors with remediation, discoverability via search, capability-based security.
